parentIntro: This week: fact families — the idea that 8 + 5 = 13 secretly contains 13 − 5 = 8. If she owns this, subtraction stops being a separate scary thing and becomes “find the missing part”. This is the foundation the big subtraction weeks stand on.
watchFor: Watch for counting one-by-one on fingers for things like 13 − 5. Don't correct it — just ask “what plus 5 makes 13?” and watch the shortcut click. The diagnostic showed her bonds are strong, so this week is about CONNECTING them to subtraction, not learning them.

demo.title: One family, four facts
demo.say: Today's secret: every adding fact has a take-away fact hiding inside it. Watch.

steps.caption: 8 and 5 — two parts
steps.say: Here are eight blue blocks and five yellow blocks. Two parts.

steps.caption: the parts make the whole
steps.say: Together the parts make thirteen. Eight plus five equals thirteen.

steps.caption: whole − one part = the other part
steps.say: Now watch. If I hide the five yellow ones — thirteen take away five — what's left is exactly the eight. The take-away was hiding inside the add!

steps.caption: one family, four facts
steps.say: Eight, five and thirteen are a fact family. One family gives us four facts for free!

weDo.problem: Build the whole fact family for 7, 6 and 13.
weDo.model: Part-part-whole drawing: a big box (the whole, 13) sitting on two small boxes (the parts, 7 and 6). Or two colours of pasta.
steps: Draw the boxes and let her place 13, 7 and 6 in the right spots.
Say a fact wrong on purpose — “13 − 6 = 8?” — and let her catch you. Kids love this.

weDo.model: Cover-up trick: write ? + 9 = 16, cover the ? with your hand and ask “what's hiding under here?”
steps: Ask her which fact family this belongs to (9, something, 16).
Flip it into a take-away together: “16 take away 9 tells us the hiding number.”
Let her find it however she likes (bridging through 10 is lovely: 9+1=10, 10+6=16, so 7).
Check by putting 7 back in: does 7 + 9 make 16? High five.

items.say: Six plus something makes ten. What is the something?

items.text: Harriet has 9 shells. She finds some more, and now she has 14. How many did she find?
items.say: Harriet has nine shells. She finds some more at the beach, and now she has fourteen. How many did she find?
What is seventeen take away eight?
Fifteen take away something leaves nine. What is the something?
Something take away seven leaves six. What is the something?

items.text: Appa bakes 25 cookies. After the family eats some, 16 are left. How many were eaten?
items.say: Appa bakes twenty five cookies. After the family eats some, sixteen are left. How many cookies were eaten?
Forty plus something makes one hundred. What is the something?

warmupWins.say: What is ten take away six?
